previous.why: Voice-defining: the cataloguing irony and self-ironizing diminution ('ten pounds of unconscious babyhood') that sets the book's register.

previous.why: States the book's premise—education as a contract one is retrospectively a party to—which the whole work returns to.

previous.why: Self-portrait catalog that establishes Adams's characterological and intellectual signature; must survive compression.

previous.why: Rare sensory/lyrical passage; the rhythm and cataloguing define a tonal high point that compression will otherwise flatten.

new.passage_hint: Had he been born in Jerusalem under the shadow of the Temple and circumcised in the Synagogue by his uncle the high priest, under the name of Israel Cohen
new.why: Famous opening conceit establishing Adams's ironic self-branding; one of the book's most-cited passages and must survive verbatim or near-verbatim.

new.passage_hint: What could become of such a child of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, when he should wake up to find himself required to play the game of the twentieth?
new.why: Sets up the book's central question and the card-game metaphor; defines the retrospective ironic voice.

new.passage_hint: He and his eighteenth-century, troglodytic Boston were suddenly cut apart—separated forever—in act if not in sentiment, by the opening of the Boston and Albany Railroad; the appearance of the first Cunard steamers
new.why: Key thematic hinge: the rupture between eighteenth and nineteenth centuries that structures the whole Education.

new.passage_hint: The habit of doubt; of distrusting his own judgment and of totally rejecting the judgment of the world; the tendency to regard every question as open; the hesitation to act except as a choice of evils
new.why: Self-catalogue of Adams's temperament in characteristic cumulative-clause rhythm; must be preserved as voice-establishing.

new.passage_hint: Resistance to something was the law of New England nature... the New Englander, whether boy or man, in his long struggle with a stingy or hostile universe, had learned also to love the pleasure of hating; his joys were few.
new.why: Signature aphoristic formulation; 'pleasure of hating' is a recurring phrase and culturally memorable characterization of New England.

new.passage_hint: To the boy Henry Adams, summer was drunken. Among senses, smell was the strongest—smell of hot pine-woods and sweet-fern in the scorching summer noon
new.why: The sensory catalogue is the most lyrical passage in the segment and establishes the winter/summer dyad; prosodically distinctive.

new.passage_hint: Winter and summer, town and country, law and liberty, were hostile, and the man who pretended they were not, was in his eyes a schoolmaster—that is, a man employed to tell lies to little boys.
new.why: Crystallizes the 'double nature' thesis and Adams's attitude toward formal education; signature aphorism.

new.passage_hint: Putting on his hat, he took the boy's hand without a word, and walked with him, paralyzed by awe, up the road to the town.
new.why: The anthologized anecdote of John Quincy Adams marching the boy to school — a core memorable scene of the segment.

new.passage_hint: he had uttered no syllable of revolting cant about the duty of obedience and the wickedness of resistance to law... the stoniest glacial and tidal drift known in any Puritan land.
new.why: The ironic meditation following the school incident — classic Adams third-person-self analysis with characteristic sting.

new.passage_hint: From cradle to grave this problem of running order through chaos, direction through space, discipline through freedom, unity through multiplicity, has always been, and must always be, the task of education
new.why: States the unity/multiplicity theme that drives the entire book toward Chartres and the Dynamo chapters; essential thematic seed.

new.passage_hint: She was Louis Seize, like the furniture... an exotic, like her Sevres china... he was not of pure New England stock, but half exotic.
new.why: The Madam portrait and the 'quarter taint of Maryland blood' — Adams's self-placement as partly alien to New England, thematically load-bearing.

new.passage_hint: would he have quitted his eighteenth-century, his ancestral prejudices, his abstract ideals, his semi-clerical training, and the rest, in order to perform an expiatory pilgrimage to State Street, and ask for the fatted calf of his grandfather Brooks and a clerkship in the Suffolk Bank?
new.why: Closing ironic coda of the chapter; trademark Adams retrospective irony and the State Street vs. Quincy dilemma that frames the book.

notes_previous: This chapter is both the book's overture and a signature voice-establishing segment—compress the genealogical/biographical middle (Louisa Catherine's travels, consular/diplomatic history) aggressively, but protect: (1) the opening 'Israel Cohen' conceit verbatim; (2) the self-characterological catalog ('habit of doubt...'); (3) the summer/smell lyrical passage; (4) the grandfather-to-school anecdote including its ironic moral; (5) the gardener's 'President too' line; (6) the death of J.Q. Adams as the closing hinge and the State Street/Suffolk Bank coda. Preserve Adams's third-person self-reference ('the boy,' 'Henry Adams,' 'the child') without slippage to first person. Keep the doubleness motif (winter/summer, town/country, Boston/Quincy) legible since later chapters echo it. Louisa Catherine's biography can be reduced to a paragraph so long as the 'half exotic / curse of Abel' interpretive beat survives. Do not modernize 'troglodytic,' 'Louis Seize,' 'Queen Anne'—they carry the period texture.
notes_new: This is the book's opening chapter and establishes voice, the card-game/education metaphor, the eighteenth/nineteenth century rupture, and the unity/multiplicity problem that returns in the signature late chapters. Preserve the third-person self-reference ('the boy,' 'Henry Adams,' 'the child') absolutely. Keep cumulative semicolon-strung catalogues intact where flagged — flattening them destroys Adams's rhythm. The JQA-school anecdote should be rendered close to full; the Madam's biographical paragraph (Berlin, St. Petersburg, White House) can be compressed to its arc but must retain 'Louis Seize, like the furniture' and the 'quarter taint of Maryland blood' line. The opening 'Jerusalem/Israel Cohen' conceit is period-typical and cannot be sanitized; render as Adams wrote it. Sensory summer catalogue is a lyrical peak — keep its texture even if some items are pruned.
